author: ValWood
body:
Hi @deustp01 

Note that 
GO:0043687 post-translational protein modification
should be blocked for direct annotation (and probably relabelled because single step modifications will only be represented in the MF branch). The only remaining processes will be those that are multistep pathways.

This change was decided back in Montreal, but the implementations have been ongoing for a number of years.

So any annotation moved up to GO:0043687 post-translational protein modification will need to be moved again.

Do you have any examples that you cannot reannotate to an appropriate process term?
The first 4 are methylases, so they do not need "methylation" as a process.

author: deustp01
body:
> Note that
> GO:0043687 post-translational protein modification
> should be blocked for direct annotation (and probably relabelled because single step modifications will only be represented in the MF branch). The only remaining processes will be those that are multistep pathways.

I applied GO:0043687 only to a Reactome pathway, "protein methylation". This pathway is a grouping of reactions that each mediate post-translational methylation of a protein or proteins, enabled by various gene products under various physiological conditions. (The individual reactions with their individual gene products have all been re-annotated, as above, to assign BP terms that point to the process that is modulated as a result of the methylation.)

I can think of no other GO BP term to apply to the grouping pathway. If the decision of current GO senior management is that grouping pathways are out of scope for GO, then the Reactome:GO mismatch can be cured by simply not assigning GO BP terms to Reactome grouping pathways. If, however, grouping pathways are in scope then terms like GO:0043687 post-translational protein modification (and, for that matter, "protein methylation") will continue to be needed for this specific kind of annotation.

@pgaudet @thomaspd opinions?

author: ValWood
body:
Hi @deustp01  I'll wait for  @pgaudet  and @thomaspd  to chip in, 
but  if you need it only for a grouping term, can you use the MF term to group?
GO:0008276  protein methyltransferase activity.
Essentially, these  operate in different pathways/processes, so a BP grouping based only on the modification would be out of scope.

author: deustp01
body:
> can you use the MF term to group?

No, because of the structure of our data model. A pathway contains multiple reactions which can be either parts_of a process or examples (is_a) of it, and the pathway must be annotated with a BP term - MF is not allowed. No term at all is allowed so that is a fix, at the cost of losing useful information.
